content.value_statement: Large Logseq template graphs can become hard to organize and maintain. This skill checks module balance, documentation, and structure, then recommends focused refactoring steps.
actual_capabilities: Counts classes and properties across Logseq module directories.
Calculates module health scores from size, documentation, completeness, and ratio rules.
Identifies bloated, small, empty, and undocumented modules.
Produces summary tables with per-module scores and status labels.
Suggests practical module split, merge, and documentation improvements.
limitations: Designed for the Logseq Template Graph source layout.
Health scores are heuristic and require human review.
Dependency analysis depends on available module references and git history.
The included scripts read local project files and do not modify modules.

use_cases.title: Review module balance before release
use_cases.description: Check whether modules are too large, too small, or missing documentation before publishing graph changes.

use_cases.title: Plan a refactoring sprint
use_cases.description: Find overloaded modules and create a prioritized plan for splitting or merging module groups.

use_cases.title: Track graph structure over time
use_cases.description: Compare module counts and health trends to understand how the template graph is evolving.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic health check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of the current module layout.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess the current Logseq module health. Show module scores, major issues, and the top three fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Explain weak modules
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review focused on the lowest scoring modules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the modules with the weakest health scores. Explain why each module is weak and suggest a practical next step.

prompt_templates.title: Design a split plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a bloated module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the largest module in detail. Group its classes by theme and propose a staged split plan with effort estimates.

prompt_templates.title: Compare architecture changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review using project history and current structure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare module health with recent history. Highlight growth trends, regressions, and refactoring work that changed the score.

output_examples.input: Check module health and summarize the main risks.
output_examples.output: A module health report with overall score, per-module status, bloated modules, small modules, and prioritized recommendations.

output_examples.input: Analyze the misc module and suggest a reorganization.
output_examples.output: A refactoring plan that groups classes by domain, names candidate modules, and estimates migration effort.

output_examples.input: Show whether module documentation is complete.
output_examples.output: A documentation review that lists missing README files and explains which modules need clearer purpose statements.

best_practices: Run the health check before major schema or module releases.
Review score changes with the module owner before moving classes.
Use recommendations as planning input, not as automatic approval.
anti_patterns: Do not split modules only to improve a numeric score.
Do not ignore common module exceptions when reviewing property counts.
Do not treat generated recommendations as a replacement for domain review.

faq.question: What project layout does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It expects a Logseq Template Graph layout with modules under a source directory.

faq.question: Does the skill change module files?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow and scripts inspect files and print recommendations.

faq.question: What does the health score measure?
faq.answer: It measures module size, documentation, completeness, and class-to-property balance using defined heuristics.

faq.question: Can it detect dependency problems?
faq.answer: It can guide dependency review when references and project history are available.

faq.question: Can teams adjust the scoring rules?
faq.answer: Yes. The scoring guidance is explicit, so teams can adapt thresholds to their project.

faq.question: Is this useful outside Logseq projects?
faq.answer: It may help with ideas, but its checks are tailored to Logseq Template Graph modules.
